answers.label: Cerebrum
answers.desc: large part of the vertebrate brain containing the cerebral cortex

answers.label: Cerebellum
answers.desc: region of the brain connected to the brainstem that coordinates motor functions and muscle tone, helping an animal's need to track moving objects, its own movements, and to analyse the sensory consequences of movements in order to control movements

answers.label: Medulla oblongata
answers.desc: structure of the brainstem that joins your spinal cord to the rest of the brain and it is responsible to involuntary functions like breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure. It also integrates sensory and motor signals and coordinates reflexes.

answers.label: Pons
answers.desc: region of the brainstem that includes neural pathways and tracts that conduct signals from the brain down to the cerebellum and medulla, and that carry the sensory signals up into the thalamus.

answers.label: Thalamus
answers.desc: part of the brain responsible for sleep regulation and relaying sensory signals. It is you your body's information relay station, where all information from your body's senses (except smell) must be processed through.

answers.label: Hypothalamus
answers.desc: a small area in the center of the brain that is part of diencephalon. It helps produce hormones that regulate heart rate, body temperature, hunger, and the sleep-wake cycle.

answers.label: Pituitary gland
answers.desc: endocrine gland at the base of the brain. Referred to as the “master gland” because it monitors and regulates many bodily functions through the hormones that it produces, including growth and sexual/reproductive development and function.

answers.label: Pineal gland
answers.desc: small endocrine gland found in most vertebrates, which produces melatonin; in humans, located in the epithalamus, in a groove where the two halves of the thalamus join; its shape and size resembles a pine nut, after which it is named

answers.label: Hippocampus
answers.desc: brain region that is part of the limbic system

answers.label: Amygdala
answers.desc: almond-shaped group of neurons in the medial temporal lobes of the brain which plays a central role in the processing and memory of emotions, especially fear

answers.label: Cerebral cortex
answers.desc: outer layer of neural tissue of the cerebrum of the brain

answers.label: Frontal lobe
answers.desc: part of the brain that, because of how large it is, it's responsible for many functions, such as motor control, executive functions, language production, emotional regulation, working memory, and personality

answers.label: Parietal lobe
answers.desc: part of the brain responsible for sensory input and some language processing

answers.label: Temporal lobe
answers.desc: part of the brain responsible for processing auditory information and encoding of memory. The temporal lobe also plays a role in processing affect/emotions, language, and certain aspects of visual perception.

answers.label: Occipital lobe
answers.desc: Part of the brain that is located at the back of the head and is responsible for visual perception. That includes colour, form and motion. Damage to the occipital lobe can cause difficulty with locating objects in environment.

answers.label: Prefrontal cortex
answers.desc: part of brain largely responsible for personality, decision making, and social behaviour

answers.label: Visual cortex
answers.desc: region of the brain that processes visual information

answers.label: Basal ganglia
answers.desc: subcortical nuclei, of varied origin, in the brains of vertebrates

answers.label: Caudate nucleus
answers.desc: one of the structures that make up the corpus striatum, which is a component of the basal ganglia

answers.label: Putamen
answers.desc: round structure located at the base of the forebrain

answers.label: Nucleus accumbens
answers.desc: region in the human basal forebrain rostral to the preoptic area of the hypothalamus

answers.label: Cingulate gyrus
answers.desc: part of the brain within the cerebral cortex

answers.label: Olfactory bulb
answers.desc: neural structure of the vertebrate forebrain involved in olfaction, which sends olfactory information to be further processed in the amygdala, the orbitofrontal cortex and the hippocampus where it plays a role in emotion, memory and learning

answers.label: Choroid plexus
answers.desc: structure in the ventricles of the brain

answers.label: Meninges
answers.desc: soft, protective membranes covering the central nervous system

answers.label: Arachnoid mater
answers.desc: weblike middle layer of the three meninges

answers.label: Pia mater
answers.desc: delicate innermost layer of the meninges, the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord

answers.label: Gyrus
answers.desc: outward fold on the brain surface

answers.label: Septum pellucidum
answers.desc: thin membrane between the lateral ventricles of the brain

answers.label: Central sulcus
answers.desc: prominent landmark of the brain (primary motor cortex), separating the parietal lobe from the frontal lobe and the primary motor cortex from the primary somatosensory cortex.

answers.label: Lateral sulcus
answers.desc: fold of the brain (primary motor cortex) separating the frontal and parietal lobes superiorly from the temporal lobe inferiorly.
